# Esther Chapter 2 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 456v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EST_002_page_001.jpg

---

**2:1** After these things [hadevarim], when the wrath [chamat] of King Ahasuerus subsided [kashokh], he remembered [zakhar] Vashti and what she had done, and what had been decreed [nigzar] against her.

**2:2** And the servants [na'arei] of the king who attended [mesharetav] him said, "Let young women [ne'arot], virgins [betulot], good [tovot] of appearance [mareh], be sought [yevaqshu] for the king.

**2:3** And let the king appoint [veyafqed] commissioners [peqidim] in all the provinces of his kingdom, and let them gather [veyiqbetzu] every young woman, a virgin, good of appearance, to Susa the citadel, to the house of the women [beit hannashim], under the custody [yad] of Hegai [Hege], the king's eunuch [seris], the keeper [shomer] of the women, and let their cosmetics [tamruqeihen] be given to them.

**2:4** And let the young woman [hanna'arah] who is good [tittov] in the eyes of the king reign [timlokh] instead of Vashti." And the thing [haddavar] was good [vayyitav] in the eyes of the king, and he did so.

**2:5** There was a man [ish], a Jew [yehudi], in Susa the citadel, and his name was Mordecai [Mordekhai], son of Jair [Ya'ir], son of Shimei [Shim'i], son of Kish [Qish], a Benjaminite [ish yemini],

**2:6** who had been exiled [hoghlah] from Jerusalem with the exile [hagolah] that had been exiled with Jeconiah [Yekhonyah] king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar [Nevukhadnetztzar] king of Babylon [Bavel] had exiled [heglah].

**2:7** And he was raising [omen] Hadassah — she is Esther [Ester] — the daughter of his uncle [dodo], for she had no father [av] and no mother [em]. And the young woman was beautiful [yefat] of form [to'ar] and good [tovat] of appearance [mareh], and at the death of her father and her mother, Mordecai took her to himself as a daughter [levat].

**2:8** And it was, when the word [devar] of the king and his decree [dato] were heard [behishama], and when many young women were gathered to Susa the citadel under the custody [yad] of Hegai, that Esther was taken [vattillaqach] to the house of the king, under the custody of Hegai, keeper of the women.

**2:9** And the young woman was good [vatittav] in his eyes and she lifted up [vattissa] covenant-faithfulness [chesed] before him, and he hastened [vayevahel] her cosmetics [tamruqeha] and her portions [manoteha] to give to her, and the seven young women [ne'arot] chosen [hare'uyot] to give to her from the house of the king, and he moved her [vayeshaneha] and her young women to the best place [letov] of the house of the women.

**2:10** Esther did not declare [lo higgidah] her people [ammah] or her kindred [moladtah], for Mordecai had commanded [tzivvah] her not to declare it.

**2:11** And every day [uvkhol yom vayom], Mordecai would walk [mithalekh] before the court [chatzer] of the house of the women, to know [lada'at] the welfare [shelom] of Esther and what would be done with her.

**2:12** And when the turn [tor] of each young woman came to go in to King Ahasuerus, after it had been done to her according to the regulation [kedat] of the women — twelve months [shnem asar chodesh], for thus were the days of their beautification [meruqeihen] fulfilled: six months with oil [shemen] of myrrh [hammor], and six months with spices [besamim] and cosmetics [tamruqei] of women —

**2:13** and with this the young woman would go in to the king: whatever she said would be given to her, to go with her from the house of the women to the house of the king.

**2:14** In the evening [ba'erev] she would go in, and in the morning [uvabboqer] she would return to the second house of the women, under the custody of Shaashgaz, the king's eunuch, keeper of the concubines [happilagshim]. She would not come again to the king unless the king delighted [chafetz] in her and she was called [veniqre'ah] by name [beshem].

**2:15** And when the turn of Esther — the daughter of Abihail [Avichayil], the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her as a daughter — came to go in to the king, she asked for nothing [lo viqshah davar] except what Hegai, the king's eunuch, keeper of the women, advised [yomar]. And Esther lifted up [noset] favor [chen] in the eyes of all who saw her.

**2:16** And Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus, to his royal house [beit malkhuto], in the tenth month [bachodesh ha'asiri] — that is, the month of Tevet [chodesh Tevet] — in the seventh year of his reign.

**2:17** And the king loved [vayyehav] Esther more than all the women, and she lifted up [vattissa] favor [chen] and covenant-faithfulness [chesed] before him more than all the virgins, and he placed [vayyasem] the royal crown [keter malkhut] on her head, and he made her queen [vayyamlikheha] instead of Vashti.

**2:18** And the king made a great feast [mishteh gadol] for all his officials and servants — the feast of Esther [mishteh Ester] — and he proclaimed a release [hanachah] for the provinces and gave gifts [mas'et] according to the hand [keyad] of the king.

**2:19** And when the virgins were gathered a second time, Mordecai was sitting [yoshev] in the gate [sha'ar] of the king.

**2:20** Esther had not declared her kindred [moladtah] or her people [ammah], as Mordecai had commanded her, for Esther was doing [osah] the command [ma'amar] of Mordecai just as when she was in his care [be'omnah].

**2:21** In those days, while Mordecai was sitting in the gate of the king, Bigthan [Bigtan] and Teresh [Teresh], two of the king's eunuchs [sarisim], from the keepers [mishshomerei] of the threshold [hassaf], became angry [vayiqtzof] and sought [vayevaqshu] to send [lishloach] a hand [yad] against King Ahasuerus.

**2:22** And the matter [haddavar] became known [vayyivvada] to Mordecai, and he told [vayyagged] it to Queen Esther, and Esther told the king in the name [beshem] of Mordecai.

**2:23** And the matter was investigated [vayyevuqqash] and found to be so [vayyimmatze], and the two of them were hanged [vayyittalu] on a tree [al etz], and it was written [vayyikkatev] in the book [besefer] of the chronicles [divrei hayyamim] before the king.

---

## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **Chesed (2:9, 2:17):** The term [chesed] appears twice in this chapter, describing what Esther "lifted up" (gained) before Hegai and before the king. This word carries the full weight of "covenant-faithfulness" or "steadfast love" — a deeply theological term used without explicit divine reference, yet suggesting that Esther's favor is more than mere charm.

2. **Hoghlah (2:6):** The genealogical note connecting Mordecai's family to the Babylonian exile under Jeconiah (597 BCE) situates the narrative within the larger story of Israel's displacement. The chronology is compressed — if taken literally, Mordecai himself was exiled, which would make him over 100 years old. Most likely the relative clause refers to Kish, his great-grandfather.

3. **Al etz (2:23):** Literally "on a tree/wood." This likely refers to impalement on a stake, the standard Persian method of execution, rather than hanging by a rope. The same phrase will recur critically later in the narrative.

*— EMET*
